pages.text: toNeko's genetics system follows $(#FF69B4)Mendelian inheritance$().$(br2)If you remember the pea plant experiments from biology class — yes, that's exactly the principle! Each neko inherits half their genes from each parent, with dominant genes suppressing recessive ones.

pages.title: Gene Structure Hierarchy
pages.text: A neko's genes are organized in these layers:$(br2)$(li)$(#FF69B4)Allele$(): the smallest hereditary unit, determines a specific trait (like "fast" or "slow")$(li)$(#FF69B4)Locus$(): each locus holds one allele, like a "slot"$(li)$(#FF69B4)Chromosome Pair$(): a chromosome contains multiple loci, paired up$(li)$(#FF69B4)Karyotype$(): a neko's complete chromosome map — $(#FF69B4)9 chromosome pairs$() in total

pages.title: Dominance & Recessiveness
pages.text: Each locus has a pair of alleles (one from each parent), but only the $(#FF69B4)more dominant one$() gets expressed.$(br2)$(li)High-dominance genes (e.g. 20) override low-dominance genes (e.g. 5~10)$(li)$(thing)Wild Type$() has dominance 10 — most nekos carry it by default, producing no effect$(li)Some rare traits (large body, resistances, luck, large chest) have only dominance 5, making them $(#FF69B4)recessive$() — only expressed when two recessive genes meet$(li)When dominance is equal, expression is $(#FF69B4)randomly chosen$()

pages.title: Inheritance Process
pages.text: Here's how genes are passed down during breeding:$(br2)$(li)Parents each produce a gamete through $(#FF69B4)meiosis$() — one chromosome randomly chosen from each pair$(li)Paternal gamete + maternal gamete $(#FF69B4)combine$(), forming the offspring's chromosome pairs$(li)Offspring genome = half from father + half from mother$(br2)Since each chromosome pair is chosen independently, the offspring's trait combinations can vary wildly — this is the "independent assortment" of Mendel's laws in action!
